msg: ElastiCache Redis OSS {v} left standard support on January 31, 2026. Since February 1, 2026 each node is billed Extended Support: an 80% premium on the on-demand node price in years 1-2, 160% from February 1, 2028; after January 31, 2029 AWS upgrades it to Valkey itself.

ElastiCache Redis OSS {v} leaves standard support on January 31, 2027. From February 1, 2027 each node is billed Extended Support (80% premium in years 1-2, 160% from February 1, 2029). Moving to Valkey now avoids it.

A redis{v} parameter group only attaches to a Redis OSS {m} cache, so it holds the cache on a version billed Extended Support since February 1, 2026. Create a valkey8 parameter group and point the cache at it in the same change.
A redis{v} parameter group ties the cache to the Redis OSS engine. Switching the engine to Valkey needs a valkey8 (or valkey7) parameter group; the redis family cannot be reused.
This ElastiCache Serverless cache runs the redis engine. AWS prices ElastiCache Serverless for Valkey 33% lower than the other supported engines.
This node-based ElastiCache cache runs the redis engine ({v}). AWS prices node-based ElastiCache for Valkey 20% lower than the other supported engines.

Image {img} is Redis 7.4 or later, which ships under RSALv2/SSPLv1 (Redis 8 adds AGPLv3), not the BSD-3 licence of Redis 7.2 and earlier. Valkey, the Linux Foundation fork of Redis 7.2.4, stays BSD-3 and speaks the same protocol.

redis/redis-stack bundles the Redis modules (search, JSON, bloom), which were never BSD-licensed. Valkey ships its own valkey-json, valkey-bloom and valkey-search modules; check each command you use before swapping.
